mcat_description.short: Office Cabin is a prefabricated, portable modular structure built with a steel (MS/GI) frame and insulated wall panels, sold as a complete ready-to-install unit for use as a temporary or semi-permanent office workspace.
mcat_description.long: Office Cabins are factory-manufactured, relocatable structures assembled from mild steel or galvanised iron frames combined with insulated sandwich panels (PUF, EPS, glass wool, or rock wool core) to create functional, weather-resistant workspaces. They are available in standard catalogue sizes (typically 8×8 ft to 40×10 ft) or custom dimensions, and can be equipped with electrical fittings, aluminium sliding windows, doors, AC provisions, and interior finishes such as vinyl flooring or MDF panelling. In the Indian B2B market, these cabins are primarily sold as site offices for construction and infrastructure projects, but also serve as security cabins, manager cabins, portable conference rooms, and temporary administrative offices. They are transported via trailer or crane and require no major civil foundation work, making them a cost-effective alternative to permanent construction for project-duration deployments.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'Office Cabin' commercially refers to a prefabricated portable modular structure — not an interior furniture partition — built on a mild steel (MS) or galvanised iron (GI) frame with insulated sandwich panel walls (PUF, EPS, glass wool, or rock wool core). The dominant construction type is the MS frame cabin with PUF or sandwich panel cladding, widely sold by manufacturers concentrated in Maharashtra (Thane, Pune), Karnataka (Bengaluru), Gujarat (Vadodara, Ahmedabad), and Delhi-NCR (Gurgaon, Noida). Key buyer vocabulary includes 'porta cabin', 'portable office cabin', 'readymade office cabin', and 'container office cabin' — the last being a high-intent sub-segment where shipping container conversions or container-style steel structures are used. Standard commercial sizes range from 8×8 ft (small security/manager cabin) to 40×10 ft (large site office block), with 10×10 and 10×20 ft being the most commonly listed catalogue sizes. Wall panel materials vary: PUF (polyurethane foam) sandwich panels offer superior thermal insulation; EPS (expanded polystyrene) panels are more economical; glass wool and rock wool are used for fire-rated applications. Flooring is typically plywood or cement board with vinyl/PVC finish. Electrical fittings (ISI-marked wiring, MCB boards, fans, tube lights) and aluminium sliding windows are standard inclusions. The market also includes a rental/hire segment (per month basis) serving short-duration project sites. Certifications observed in the market include ISO 9001:2015 and ISI-marked steel; no specific BIS standard exclusively governs portable office cabins as a product category — they are governed by the standards of their constituent materials (IS 2062 for structural steel, IS 277 for GI sheets). The 'container office cabin' sub-segment (keyword: 33 pageviews, 10 calls — highest call conversion) represents a premium, durable variant using shipping container-grade steel structures.
